prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S129: The Drone Tasking Service converts reconnaissance objectives into trackable missions with launch windows, image requirements, altitude limits, and abort criteria.
S130: Horizon Ridge Drone Dock supports initial attack by keeping assigned aircraft charged, positioned, and ready for rapid launch when mission approval is granted.
S131: Kestrel is required to report launch readiness, aircraft health, and recovery availability before a reconnaissance task can be released.
S132: The Drone Pilot Operator confirms that the proposed route is consistent with field conditions and can be flown without interfering with suppression aircraft.
S133: Reconnaissance imagery is used to verify access, flame spread direction, and exposure to structures before crews are committed to a line assignment.
S134: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine compares recent reconnaissance observations with camera detections and weather-driven projections to support tactical recommendations.
S135: The Smoke Classifier Module remains a supporting source during suppression planning and is not treated as the sole basis for aircraft commitment.
S136: The Air Attack Supervisor uses the Wind Shift Bulletin to reassess aircraft sequencing, holding areas, and drop approach direction.
S137: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console maintains a planning view of tanker availability, estimated time to target, base turnaround time, and assigned incident priority.
S138: Marigold must prevent a dispatch plan from being released when required aviation approvals, airspace status, or tanker readiness fields are incomplete.
S139: The Airspace Restricted State limits dispatch options until the Air Attack Supervisor confirms that the planned route and working altitude are acceptable.
S140: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console produces the Runway Release Note after the planned departure sequence has been validated against runway constraints.
S141: The Tanker Base Manager uses the batch slip to confirm that the loading record matches the aircraft assignment and planned retardant quantity.
S142: The East Retardant Loading Pump and West Retardant Loading Pump report equipment state, flow readiness, and out-of-service conditions to support base capacity estimates.
S143: Loading status is displayed as operational information rather than as an approval, so a supervisor decision is still required before aircraft are committed.
S144: The Tanker Base Manager resolves discrepancies in loading status before the dispatch plan is presented as ready for release.
S145: The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater provides an operational fallback for relaying approved aviation instructions when data connectivity is degraded.
S146: The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
S147: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
S148: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
S149: During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
S150: The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
S151: If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
S152: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
S153: When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
S154: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
S155: The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
S156: The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
S157: Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
S158: Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
S159: The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
S160: If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
S161: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
S162: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
S163: The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.
S164: Lantern issues a crew exposure refresh only after the current reconnaissance confidence and weather timing fields are both valid.
